text: Manage nodes, groups and rules Use the Routing hub to add node sources, choose how groups select nodes and decide which traffic uses them. This guide covers the standard edition; for an end-to-end example, follow Route your first connection. Task Page Check before starting Add or edit a subscription or node Nodes Node management Refresh a subscription Nodes Subscription refresh Choose a member or pin an automatic group Policies Group selection Change membership or group settings Policies Group editing Test a node or group Nodes or Policies Latency probes Apply a template or edit rules Rules Rules and templates Add rules for common services Service rules Rules and templates Simulate a route Trace simulation Routing trace See what doona can change for when a change takes effect. Open the help beside an unavailable control to find its reason. Add and maintain nodes Open Nodes. Select a source card to see its nodes; use the table's search and filters to find a node. The Latency tab compares available measurements. Search nodes searches every source; Group and Protocol filter the table. A reported stream transport appears after the protocol, while filtering still matches the protocol. Source cards show kind, state, node count, update times, expiry and usage. A quota meter appears when the backend reports an allowance. Expiry shows minutes, with seconds in its tooltip. Arrow keys move between cards. Not fetched means no successful fetch and no reported error; Stale means retained data needs updating. Empty file sources remain listed with their status. Latency shows the lowest and highest latency and unavailable-node count. Compare Latest latency with Moving average and Average of the last 10 when reported. Group by groups nodes by group or protocol and names unavailable or unmeasured nodes. Selecting a chart node opens it on Nodes. Add a subscription Choose Add subscription. Enter Name and Subscription URL. Review Auto-update, User-Agent and Cache the subscription if offered. Choose Add. When subscription refresh is available, doona fetches the new source and reports the node count. If that fetch fails, use Retry in the notice. Select the source card and check its nodes before creating a group. Subscription URLs must use HTTP or HTTPS. doona adds https:// to a URL without a scheme when the field loses focus or you save it. Invalid URLs and node links show an explanation below their fields. Add node links Choose Paste node link. For one link, enter Name and Node link. For several links, paste one per line and review the parsed names and errors. Confirm the addition and check the result. If some links fail, the dialog keeps them for correction. honk supports XHTTP over H2 for Trojan, VMess and VLESS links. xhttp and splithttp select this transport; supported modes are auto, packet-up, stream-up and stream-one. See honk’s XHTTP reference for supported options and limits. Refresh or edit a subscription Use the update action on its source card to fetch it now. The page's subscription update button refreshes all subscriptions. To change the URL or options, use the card's edit action. Change the offered fields, then choose Apply. If the card instead offers Open config file, edit the declaration there. Use Auto-update to choose an interval. For Custom, enter a non-negative whole Interval and choose its Unit. If Download route appears, choose the route for fetching the subscription. It does not set the route for traffic using its nodes. A failed refresh keeps the last successfully loaded nodes. If the selected download route has no usable node, the refresh fails instead of falling back to direct. This can happen when a subscription routes through nodes it has not delivered yet. An empty User-Agent removes ua and uses the engine default. Cache the subscription appears when the entry sets cache or the backend reports a cache default. Choosing By routing rules removes the explicit route. Other options stay as written. Renaming can update simple subtag(...) filters in the same file. Keep the offered update switch on to retain those group memberships. References in another file or inside an expression block renaming. If group filters block a rename, follow the dialog's links to Policies and update those filters first. For failed downloads, check the subscription refresh requirements. Edit or remove a node source Use a source card's More actions menu to remove the source, then review the confirmation. If groups still refer to a subscription, the dialog names them; change their filters first. For a node declared in configuration, use the row's edit or remove action when offered. If a declaration belongs to an include file and removal is unavailable, open that file in Configuration. Select rows with their checkboxes to work on several nodes at once. Every row can be selected, including subscription and include-file nodes. With a selection, Test all becomes Test selected (N) and tests only those nodes. Remove selected (N) counts only the manual nodes in the main configuration that you can remove; subscription and include-file nodes are never removed. One confirmation removes them one at a time and shows progress. Closing the dialog stops the remaining removals, and nodes that fail stay selected. Ctrl A or ⌘A selects every listed row, Shift with ↑ or ↓ extends the selection, and Esc clears it. Changing the source, search or filters clears the selection. Renaming an inline node updates exact node filters, default and final members, and DNS upstream detours in its declaring source. References from another source prevent renaming. Add to group opens the group editor with the node staged; Apply confirms. It lists groups in writable main or include files and supports search. Group editing can use readable configuration even when the runtime groups API is unavailable. Choose and edit policy groups Open Policies. Each card represents a group; expand a folded card to see its members. The card shows the selected member and the reported health of its members. All, Manual and Automatic filter groups by selection kind and show counts. The filter stays in the URL; opening a hidden group returns to All. Cards show the policy and available, unavailable and untested counts. Groups with more than 12 members offer Filter nodes, Region, Sort and Available only. Automatic groups start folded; pinned groups and groups opened by a link expand automatically. A nested group shows the parent’s latency sample for it, or the latency of the node its current selection resolves to. Choose a member If the card offers Both, TCP and UDP, select the network to change. Choose a member. A manual group selects it; an automatic group that allows overrides pins it and shows Pinned. To remove a pin, choose Back to automatic from More actions. On an expanded card this follows the selected network; on a folded automatic card it clears both pins. For selections across restarts, see persistence requirements. Create or edit a group Choose New group, or use a card's pencil button to edit that group. For a new group, enter Group name. Choose Selection policy. Select regions, subscriptions, nodes or nested groups to include. Review Matching nodes before saving. An empty filter includes all nodes. Use Add filter for conditions not covered by the membership choices. Conditions within a filter must all match; Add OR match adds an alternative. Review Default member, Final outbound and the connection-interruption switch when offered. The default is the initial member for manual selection. The group uses the final outbound when no member is available. Choose Create for a new group or Apply for an edit, then check the result. Cancel abandons the draft after any discard confirmation. Removing an explicit member does not exclude it if another filter still matches it. Change that filter too. For read-only fields, see group editing requirements. Default member appears only for manual selection and lists direct members. Choosing an automatic policy leaves the stored default unchanged. Final outbound offers direct, block, groups and nodes, excluding groups that would form a cycle. None removes the corresponding default or final setting. Interrupt existing connections on switch controls whether selecting another member closes existing connections. In Edit group, it waits for Apply. In View configuration, changing the switch writes immediately. After a configuration conflict, retrying preserves fields you did not edit. Reopen the editor if edits conflict or the group has a new name. If someone removed the group elsewhere, the editor stays open and reports that it did not save the changes. Expand Regions to choose regions; selected tags stay visible. Add filter supports name and subtag matches, and custom expressions remain editable as text. In the Groups and Nodes pickers, search stays fixed while the options scroll. Test members or change background checks Use a group’s More actions → Test all, or a node’s test button, to use your manual probe preferences. Choose Probe with options… to adjust one test. Check probe requirements if the action is unavailable. On Nodes, Test all in the toolbar tests the listed nodes. A timed-out or cancelled measurement, an unavailable address or a local refusal can leave a result unknown. This does not prove that the node is unavailable. Trojan, AnyTLS and VLESS retain DNS UDP probe choices whose support depends on node configuration. doona reports backend admission refusals instead of silently falling back to HTTP. For a group's background checks, choose More actions → Check settings, edit the offered fields and choose Apply. These settings are separate from a manual test. Leave a check field empty to remove the group override and use the global value or default. After a conflict, unchanged fields take the backend’s new values. Fields changed on both sides keep your draft and show the backend value beside it; applying again replaces that value. Apply a routing template Open Rules → Routing rules. When the view switch appears, use Simple for templates and Advanced for the rule list. See rule and template requirements before applying a template. You can inspect templates from readable configuration even without the rules API. Simple is the default unless a link selects a rule, prefills a new rule or reviews held rules. Custom routing and routing spread over several files have no selected template. Routing mode offers Bypass mainland China, GFW list only and Global proxy. More templates offers Single proxy group, Groups by service, Groups by service and region, and Back to mainland China. Back to mainland China sends mainland Chinese domains and IPs through group cn. That group's name matching excludes Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan. Other traffic goes direct. Choose a Routing mode, or open More templates for additional choices. Review the template description and options. Choose Apply to open the confirmation. Review the target file, groups to create or reuse, and the file diff. A template replaces the target file's top-level routing rules. Routing includes removed by that replacement stop contributing rules through those statements; the included files remain on disk. If Also add DNS routing appears, decide whether to include the proposed DNS configuration. Confirm with Apply and check the result. If validation fails, correct the reported problem before applying again. Existing groups retain their settings. Review warnings about reused groups or names that collide with nodes before confirming. Template option Default and effect Block ads Off; blocks geosite:category-ads-all when enabled. Block QUIC On; blocks UDP port 443. honk marks its own sockets before routing, so this does not block its connections to QUIC-based nodes. Keep NetworkManager direct On; sends NetworkManager traffic direct. The defaults apply when the routing holds no rules. Otherwise each option starts from the routing. A detected template keeps its choices. For custom routing, an option starts on only when the routing already contains its rule, so applying a template keeps the ad, QUIC and NetworkManager rules unless you turn the option off. Also add DNS routing appears only when no loaded file has a dns block. The checkbox defaults to on. It sends geosite:cn queries to alidns at 223.5.5.5:53 over UDP, and other queries to cloudflare at 1.1.1.1:853 over DNS over TLS. Warnings identify reused groups that select one exact node or use a fixed policy. If a new group has the same name as a node, rules naming it reach the group instead of the node. The target is the file containing top-level routing, or the main file when none exists. doona adds missing groups there. Existing DNS routing, other content and other files stay unchanged. New group labels follow the interface language; region labels include country flags. Add service rules Add service rules in the Rules → Routing rules toolbar adds one rule per service, such as domain(geosite:netflix) -> proxy, and keeps the existing rules. Choose Add service rules, then an Outbound for all selected services. Select services under Games, Media, Social and messaging, AI and Development and platforms. Choose Apply to write the rules and reload, or Hold to add them to held rules. The dialog disables a service when a routing rule or held rule already uses its category (A rule already exists), or when the loaded geodata lacks it (Not included in the current geodata). The rules go into the file that holds the fallback, just before the fallback. The first matching rule decides, so a game service other than All games goes above an existing geosite:category-games rule in that file. Otherwise that rule would take the game's traffic. Two services add more than one rule: Steam: with an outbound other than direct or block, Connect Steam downloads directly adds domain(geosite:steam@cn) -> direct before the Steam rule. Telegram: adds dip(geoip:telegram) with the same outbound, and the DNS request rule qname(geosite: telegram) && qtype(https, svcb) -> reject unless one exists, so Telegram connections do not bypass the proxy. When the DNS request rules are in another file, the dialog says so and leaves DNS unchanged. If doona cannot write the fallback's file, the dialog reports that rules cannot be added automatically. Add them in the configuration file instead, or see rule requirements. Add or change an individual routing rule Open Rules → Routing rules → Advanced when the view switch is present. Choose Add rule. Select Match by and enter Values, separating multiple values with commas. Add AND condition adds another condition that must also match. Use Expression for a custom condition. Choose Outbound and Insert. Review earlier rules when choosing a position: the first matching rule determines the result. Choose Add rule and check the result in the list. Switching from Expression to Select converts representable expressions into condition rows; other expressions stay in Expression with a hint. Domain keyword matches a substring: tracker, ads matches either keyword. Outbound offers direct, block and groups, but not individual nodes. Turn on Lock this outbound to add must. Insert offers Last, before the fallback or a position before a listed rule, starting at the first offered position. Both pickers support search. Use a row's Edit rule to change its condition or target, then Save. Use Remove rule and confirm to delete it. The fallback row supplies the target when no preceding rule matches. If you cannot edit or remove a rule in the list, use Open config file to edit its declaring file. This action also opens read-only sources at the rule’s line. Editing a fallback changes only its target. Hits counts retained flows whose rule_generation_id matches the list’s generation_id; it is not a running total. Without a rule list, the view groups current-snapshot flows by rule and shows Hits and Share. Rule source distinguishes kernel, userspace, recomputed and unknown. Start from observed traffic Use an add-rule action on a Connections, Routing log or DNS row, or on a Trace evaluation that offers it. Review the selected rule list, condition, target and insertion position. A DNS domain can open a DNS request rule; without DNS rules it opens a routing rule. Read the preview and any duplicate-rule or earlier-rule warning. Choose Apply to write this rule, or Hold to add it to held rules. If writing is unavailable, use Copy rule. The dialog has no preset outbound. It shows the current outbound and warns when the choice would not change it. When the matched rule belongs to a writable file, Insert defaults to Before the matched rule. The other choices are Last, before the fallback and First. You can also limit DNS conditions to the query’s record type. Row icons work without selecting the row first. Connections also offers Add rule in its detail panel, but not its toolbar. Routing log uses the row icon, not its detail panel. DNS offers Add rule in query results, beside answered addresses, and on Resolution log and Cache rows. After applying, the success notice offers View rule for a routing rule, or Query again for a DNS rule added from a DNS query. Add or change a DNS rule Open Rules → DNS rules. Request rules choose how to resolve a query; response rules decide what to do with an answer. Choose Add rule under Request rules or Response rules. Select the condition and enter its values, or use Expression. Choose Action and, when requested, an upstream. To define an upstream first, follow the DNS setup example. Choose Insert, review the condition and action, then choose Add rule. Use the DNS page to query the name and inspect the result. Existing DNS rules use the same edit, save and removal controls as routing rules. See DNS rule requirements if the list or an action is unavailable. honk checks each DNS list in order. Response rules accept an answer, reject it or query another upstream. DNS rule dialogs use Action instead of Outbound and do not offer Lock this outbound. Resolution log opens DNS; Open DNS configuration opens the dns section. Apply held rules Held rules are drafts in the current page session. Reloading the browser page loses them. Open Rules and review the pending card for each list with held rules. Remove unwanted entries with Discard held rule. Choose Apply held rules, or the counted apply button in the top bar. This applies held rules from every list. Read the result. doona processes files one at a time; if a file fails, unwritten rules stay held. Rules already written leave the list even if their activation fails, so follow the failure notice before continuing. The browser asks before leaving while you have held rules. Pending cards show each rule and insertion position, identify held rules in other lists and report counts for writes to more than one file. A failed write shows its lines on the card. Reload honk reloads the configuration already stored; it does not apply held rules. Check a route with Trace Trace evaluates inputs against the current configuration. It does not test a connection to the destination. Open Rules → Trace simulation. Choose Network protocol, then enter a Domain, a Destination IP, or both, and a Destination port. Choose an offered Resolution mode. See Trace requirements for supported modes. Live resolution (live) and Resolve, then simulate (query) require a Domain and an empty Destination IP. Expand Advanced if the rules need source, process, DSCP or mark information. Fill the relevant fields. DSCP accepts an integer from 0 to 63. Choose Run trace. Read Decision, the outbound and the per-rule results. If inputs are missing, supply them and run the trace again. For a real connection, check Connections. Use an offered Add rule action on the trace result to start a rule from those inputs. An IP-only trace evaluates that IP and port. Domain-family dial_mode can discover a domain from real TLS or HTTP traffic and evaluate routing again; include the domain to simulate that. For an indeterminate result, supply any Missing inputs. doona infers Likely outbound, when shown, from a matched rule in the same generation; it does not confirm the decision. The result identifies its observation time and generation, and lists Matched, Not matched, Skipped or Indeterminate for each rule. Query resolution adds a DNS query card with Query DNS and View cache links. Group results show the group-to-node chain under Node and its Reachability, with controls to test the node or open its group and node pages.

title: Change configuration and settings
description: Edit configuration files or change settings through the standard edition of doona.
headings: Update geodata or change its sources
text: Change configuration and settings Edit configuration files or change settings through the standard edition of doona. For configuration keys and examples, use the configuration reference; for storage and activation behavior, see what doona can change. Choose a configuration editor Open Configuration from the Settings hub. Check the editing requirements if a control is unavailable. Tab Use it to Modules Find a configuration section and use Open page to reach its editor. Global settings Change offered global fields through a form. Config files Read or edit a whole source file and inspect its diagnostics. Backups and revisions Export configuration, import server files or restore a stored revision. See availability. Config version identifies the accepted configuration; the adjacent status reports diagnostics. Listener secret values are redacted means the returned text hides those values. Modules opens by default; source links and a missing main-source body open Config files. Global settings appears only for engines whose settings doona supports. Incomplete means the source text is incomplete or its SHA-256 differs from the backend's reported value. It does not by itself indicate secret redaction. You cannot edit this source in doona; edit the file on the host. For subscriptions, use Nodes. For group membership, use Policies. For routing templates and individual rules, use Rules. Edit a configuration file Open Config files and select a file from Config file. Check its badge before editing. If it is read-only, follow source permissions and refusal reasons. Edit the text. Not applied marks a draft; Cancel discards it. Choose Validate when offered, then review the diagnostics. Use Go to reach a line or Open to inspect another file. See validation requirements. Choose Apply and wait for the result. On success, the notice names the written file and confirms the reload. For an unsuccessful or unconfirmed operation, read the notice before sending another change. Reloading or closing the page loses an unapplied draft. Diagnostics distinguish the accepted configuration from the current draft; typing starts a new draft check when validation is available. The file picker identifies Main, Include, Subscription and Generated sources. Hover over the line count and size to see the loaded time. Subscription updates replace subscription sources; the engine overwrites generated sources, so edit the configuration that produces them. Typing in a read-only source shows its notice once per file. Diagnostics for the accepted configuration remain until draft validation completes. Applying a change or receiving a new accepted generation clears previous validation results. An empty level filter returns to All. Older validation links open diagnostics on Config files. If the file changes while you edit, saving pauses. Review that change before choosing Keep changes, which lets your draft replace the newer file, then Apply. Choose Cancel to discard your draft and use the newer text. A restart-required notice means honk refused the edit. Follow the restart-only settings procedure instead of repeatedly applying it. Create an included file On Config files, choose New file. If the dialog supplies the directory and extension, enter only Name. Choose Include pattern first if the dialog offers several patterns. Otherwise, enter a .dae path relative to the main configuration’s directory in Path. Resolve any warning that the path matches no loaded include pattern. Choose Create. The empty file opens in the editor; continue with the editing steps above. Use the global settings form Open Global settings and select the section to edit from Config file. Change the offered fields, following their units and ranges. Use the configuration reference to check a key's meaning; resolve duplicate entries in Config files. Choose Write and reload, or Discard changes to drop the draft. Check the result before leaving. If writing succeeds but doona cannot read back the new configuration, it keeps the draft and offers Retry. The picker includes global sections in main and include files; a main file without one can receive a new section. Not set uses the engine default. Clearing a numeric field leaves it unset; integer fields reject decimal points, and ports display ungrouped numbers such as 8080. Stored subscription bodies use the subscription_body table in the state database described in the configuration reference. Separate .sub files are legacy storage; see honk’s subscription reference for startup migration. Export or restore configuration Open Backups and revisions, then choose the task: Task Action Download accepted configuration Choose Export configuration. Review credentials before sharing the download. Replace database configuration with server files Choose Import server files, review the confirmation and confirm. This reads honk's startup file tree; it is not a local file upload. Restore a recorded revision Open the revision, review its metadata and sources, then choose Restore revision and confirm. Check an unconfirmed import or restore Use Refresh to check the accepted operation before starting another write. Review the revision’s source SHA-256 values before restoring it. If the database head changes during import or restore, review and confirm the replacement again. To download only the selected source text, use Download source file on Config files. Review that file before sharing it too. See backup and revision requirements for the available operations and export limits. Open Settings Settings has General and Appearance tabs. General contains backend profiles, temporary runtime overrides, geodata, latency probes and About. The page also opens without a connected backend. Connect or switch backends In General → Backend, select a Profile, or choose Add profile to create one. Enter Backend URL as the backend root or reverse-proxy prefix, without /api/v1. Enter mock for demo data. You cannot save an empty address. Enter Token for token authentication. For password authentication, follow the sign-in guide. Choose Test connection and read the result. Choose Save to store the profile and reload the page with it. Switching profiles or confirming a profile dialog discards unsaved address and token edits. Rename profile and Delete profile manage saved entries. Sign out ends password sign-in or removes the saved token from this browser; removing a token does not revoke it on the backend. Selecting another profile saves the choice and reloads immediately. Confirming Add profile, Rename profile or Delete profile also reloads; a new profile starts with demo data. A pairing link fills Backend URL and Token; they take effect after Save. Save changes this browser’s profile, not honk’s configuration. For test or sign-in failures, see sign-in troubleshooting. Change temporary runtime options Check the runtime override requirements first. Open Temporary runtime overrides and check whether the values are From configuration or Runtime override. Change the offered log level, record limits, flow retention or recording modes. Each recorder has its own demand-based, always-on and off choices. Choose Apply, or Discard changes to abandon the draft. Read the recording status beside each recorder. If runtime options change on the backend while you edit, doona keeps your draft and reports the change. The offered fields include Log level, Log records kept, DNS log records kept, Flows kept and Flow retention (seconds). Flow recording offers On flow demand; Log recording offers On log demand; DNS log offers On DNS log demand. Each also offers Always and Off. Recorder status reads Recording, Idle or Disabled in configuration. For how long overrides last, see runtime changes. For persistent values, use Edit persistent settings in Configuration and the configuration reference. Update geodata or change its sources Check file availability, update requirements and settings requirements for the controls you need. Open Geodata and inspect the files. Expand Details for check times and download information. To download the configured sources now, choose Update now and wait for the result. To change sources, choose a preset in Source, or choose Custom and enter the URLs. Review any missing-category warning. In the custom dialog, confirm with the available action: Apply and update or Apply. Adjust Download route, Verify checksum or Automatic updates when offered. For Specific group, select the group to save the route. These controls save on change; check each result. To remove overrides, choose Reset to defaults and review the confirmation before proceeding. Source offers Loyalsoldier, MetaCubeX full, MetaCubeX lite and Custom. With honk, each custom URL list accepts up to four URLs, tried in order. Edit reopens the custom dialog. Details shows Last checked and Next check, followed by each file’s size, download host and route. The file table shows each file’s update time. See geodata storage and activation for persistence, and geodata troubleshooting for download or activation failures. Set manual probe preferences Open Latency probes. Choose Probe method, IP family, Measurement and Group probes. Return to a node or group and use its test button. Probe with options… lets you adjust the options for that test. Warm (reuse connection) reuses a connection; Cold (new connection) opens a new connection. Group probes chooses Direct members or Every leaf node, including nested groups. See probe requirements and result meanings. For background checks, use Edit health checks in Configuration; their keys are in the configuration reference. Change appearance Open Appearance. Choose Language, Palette and Color scheme. Adjust Date format, Time format or Open at startup as needed. With a Glass palette, use Choose image under Wallpaper to select an image, or Use default to restore the built-in wallpaper. Adjust the offered veil and blur controls for readability. Date and time Date format defaults to Automatic (browser region), independently of the interface language. Day/Month/Year, Month/Day/Year and Year-Month-Day override it. Time format defaults to 24-hour. 12-hour uses the interface language's AM/PM words; Automatic (browser region) follows the browser region. These choices apply throughout the interface, including charts and the log heatmap. Layout and startup Wordmark, Notification position and Mirrored layout are also available. Mirrored layout flips the interface left to right. Show country flags controls flags before node names without changing routing. Show trends on activity cards controls traffic, CPU and latency sparklines. Open at startup defaults to Activity and saves immediately. It applies only when the address has no page route. Explicit page links keep their destination; without a configured backend, an address without a page route opens Settings. Glass and wallpaper Glass palettes are Liquid Glass, Glass, Frosted and Tinted: Firefox and Safari render Liquid Glass as Glass. See browser requirements for Liquid Glass support. Frosted uses uniform blur. Tinted has nearly opaque surfaces and no blur. Liquid Glass tables on Events and Logs omit refraction and the bright rim. Reduce Transparency, Increase Contrast and forced colors use solid surfaces. Custom wallpapers also appear behind sign-in. doona scales them to at most 2560 pixels on the long edge. Control Default or limit Readability veil On by default. Dim Defaults to its maximum of 60%; white in light mode and black in dark mode. Blur 0% to 150% for Liquid Glass, Glass and Frosted. Below 100%, surface fill increases. Tinted has no Blur control. For browser support and storage requirements, see browser settings. The storage overview explains which choices belong to this browser. Halloween Halloween is under Other in the palette list. Daylight puts pumpkin orange on parchment and Midnight puts it on deep purple. Running states read Haunting, and unavailable and degraded states read Cursed. Cards carry faint drawings of a jack-o'-lantern, bats, a black cat and a spider web, and the duck logo wears a witch's hat. Its styles load only when you choose it. Get help and error details In About, use Guide for documentation and Keyboard shortcuts for the shortcut list. Copy recent errors copies the recent API failures for a bug report; a failure notice's Copy error copies that request's details. About doona shows engine, API and contract versions, the license and privacy statement. Install as an app appears when supported. When not already running as an app, Safari on iOS/iPadOS and Safari 26 or later on macOS show manual installation steps. An API major version other than 1 produces a warning. If a read returns empty JSON or no response, doona retries it once before showing an error. Error details identify the request and key response headers. Find backend actions Action Page and instructions Requirements Reload, suspend or resume honk System status Lifecycle actions Delete DNS cache entries DNS Cache actions Refresh subscriptions Nodes Subscription refresh Close connections Connections Connection actions For writing rules held in the browser, use held rules.

title: Common tasks
description: Change routing, manage subscriptions, and diagnose traffic in the standard edition.
headings: Send one site's traffic through a proxy
Route a domain and its subdomains through a group
Make a device bypass the proxy
Choose a group's node and return to automatic selection
Find why a connection used an outbound
Reload after editing files outside doona
Resolve a file changed by another editor
text: Common tasks Change routing, manage subscriptions, and diagnose traffic in the standard edition. For a first configuration, follow Route your first connection; for the smaller edition, see doona lite. Before changing a rule, check rule editing requirements. For when a saved change takes effect, see configuration writes. Send one site's traffic through a proxy Open Connections → List and find a connection to the site. Select its add-rule icon. Set Match by to Full domain and Outbound to your proxy group. Check the preview and Insert. Place the new rule before any rule that would match the same traffic first. Select Apply and check the success notice. To collect changes before applying them, use Hold and follow held rules. To include subdomains or keep this route in Global and Direct modes, use the domain rule procedure. Route a domain and its subdomains through a group Open Rules → Routing rules. Select Advanced if the view switch appears, then Add rule. Set Match by to Domain suffix and enter the domain in Values. Set Outbound to the group. Turn on Lock this outbound if this rule must also apply in Global or Direct mode. Set Insert before any earlier rule that would match the same traffic. Select Add rule in the dialog. Check the success notice and the new rule in the list. For other conditions and rule ordering, see the rule editor. Make a device bypass the proxy Use a fixed IP address for the device so the rule continues to match it. Open Rules → Routing rules. Select Advanced if shown, then Add rule. Set Match by to Source IP and enter the device's IP address in Values. Set Outbound to direct and enable Lock this outbound. Set Insert before any rule that would match this device first. Select Add rule. Check that the new rule contains the intended source address and outbound. Use Trace simulation with that source address to check which rule wins. Choose a group's node and return to automatic selection Check selection and pinning requirements. Open Policies and expand the group's card. Select a node in its node grid. Read the notice to confirm the selection and whether the automatic policy has paused. To clear a manual pin, open the card's More actions menu and select Back to automatic. Check the member reported by the resulting notice. For group policies, see policy groups. Add or refresh a subscription Check subscription creation requirements and the separate refresh requirements. Open Nodes and select Add subscription. Enter Name and Subscription URL, then select Add. Select the new subscription card and check its nodes. If the backend supports refresh, doona requests it after adding the subscription. The notice reports the result. To refresh later, use the update button on that card. If doona saved the declaration but the refresh failed, resolve the reported error and use that button again. Continue with creating a group when the subscription has nodes. Switch to Global mode Check outbound-mode requirements. Open Activity. Select Global on Outbound mode, then choose a target on Global outbound. Select Apply and read the confirmation dialog. Select Apply in the dialog. Check the notice and the displayed mode. To return to rule-based routing, choose Rule and select Apply. Choosing a global outbound also selects Global mode. In Global mode, choose a target to enable Apply. Changing the selection alone does not apply it. Select Read-only to inspect a write restriction; Not provided by this backend means the backend offers no configuration this control can edit. Find why a connection used an outbound Open Connections → List and select the connection. Read Outbound, Chain and Rule in its details. In More actions, choose Show matched rule when available to open the matching rule. To test the current configuration, choose Trace this connection and then Run trace. A trace evaluates routing; it does not replay the connection. For availability and interpretation, see trace requirements and connection details. Check how a domain resolves Check DNS query requirements. Open DNS → Query. Enter Domain and choose Type. If Upstream appears, leave Automatic to follow the configured DNS routing, or select a named upstream. Bypass cache is off by default. Enable it when the diagnostic lookup must bypass cached answers. Select Query. Read the answers, status, upstream and routing information in the result. To inspect recorded traffic instead, open Resolution log. See DNS data and its limits. Update geodata Check manual update requirements before starting. Open Settings and find Geodata. Select Update now. Wait for the operation to finish, then check its notice and the asset details. If it fails, use the reported stage in geodata update failures. Changing sources or the schedule is a separate task: see geodata settings and where those changes are stored. Reload after editing files outside doona First check whether the setting needs a reload or a restart. The reload action also has backend requirements. Select Reload honk in the top bar. On a narrow screen, find it under More options. Select Reload honk in the confirmation dialog. Check the result notice before making another change. Reload does not apply the held rules. Use their apply action separately. Resolve a file changed by another editor Open Configuration → Config files and choose the file in Config file. If the page reports a disk change, compare your draft with the current file before deciding what to keep. To discard your draft, select Cancel. The editor returns to the current source. To replace the current source with your draft, select Keep changes, then Apply. Check the result and read the file back. Keep changes does not merge the two versions. For a refused write, see read-only files and write errors.

title: Find the right page
description: Find a task in the standard edition of doona.
headings: When a page or action is unavailable
text: Find the right page Find a task in the standard edition of doona. For a first setup, follow Quick start and Route your first connection; for the smaller interface, see doona lite. Validate routing from a real LAN client using working nodes: test direct and proxied TCP, UDP and DNS. honk-core is running, the dae0 link and a reachable API do not prove that traffic flows. Pages Page What to do there Availability Activity Watch traffic, memory, connections and node health on a dashboard. Live metrics, history System status Check the engine, datapath and explanations for limited features. Runtime status Connections Inspect live connections, their routing and traffic; close connections or open their matched rule. Connection actions Routing log Inspect recorded flows and the routing map to understand previous routing decisions. Flow recording DNS Query a name, inspect answers and cache entries, or read the resolution log. Queries, cache, log Nodes Add subscriptions or node links, refresh sources and test nodes. Node management, subscription refresh, probes Policies Choose a group's member or edit its selection policy and membership. Selection, editing Rules Apply a routing template, edit routing or DNS rules, and simulate a route. Rules and templates, Trace Configuration Open configuration modules, edit files or global settings, and manage backups and revisions. Editing, validation, revisions Events Inspect backend events. Event stream Logs Read, filter, pause and export engine logs. Log recording Settings Manage backend profiles, temporary overrides, geodata, probe preferences and appearance. The page opens without a backend. See runtime overrides, geodata and browser settings for its controls. When a page or action is unavailable Pages stay in navigation even when the backend cannot provide their data. Open System status to read the feature limitations, or open the help beside a disabled action. Follow the matching requirement link in the table before changing the backend. For an editing refusal, see read-only sources. For sign-in errors, see sign-in troubleshooting. Dashboard and floating panel Activity and the floating panel share a widget gallery. Choose cards for the values you need, such as traffic, memory, node availability, DNS latency or subscription quota. See the Activity guide for the dashboard and the panel guide for arranging the floating panel. Read quota and memory Subscription quota is not in the default layout. Add it to see expiry and an allowance meter, or usage when the backend reports no allowance. Memory defaults to a chart; Sparkline provides a value tile. In the floating panel, medium size shows resident memory and cgroup usage against its limit; the chart starts at large size. The meter uses cgroup usage and omits a zero or missing limit. The display distinguishes an unreported limit from an unset one, and Key-value list identifies reported OOM kills. Choose a size Dashboard widths range from one fifth to full width. Cumulative traffic and DNS and network splits stop at half width; the group switch stops at two thirds. Unsupported saved sizes use the nearest available size. Metric widgets in the panel omit a redundant large size. At two thirds width, charts and wide metric lists show peak and average values. Wide lists with at least four rows use two columns. Node latency adds its range at half width. Large donuts enlarge the ring and narrow the legend; large panel donuts show every entry. Narrow legends retain names, values and shares. Small panel notices take a full row, and small node latency uses names and values. Long names wrap, notices grow to fit their content, and DNS and network splits show every category. Narrow area charts omit overlapping time labels. Waiting sparklines show a baseline until a second sample arrives. Settings stored in the browser Compare the palette gallery, then change appearance settings. For language, appearance, date and time formats, startup page and probe preferences, use Settings. To distinguish browser preferences from saved configuration and temporary backend changes, see where changes are stored. This origin’s localStorage keeps profiles, tokens, preferences and layouts. Clearing browser data removes those saved browser values, not honk’s configuration. sessionStorage keeps per-tab state such as each section’s last page. Token requests use Authorization; doona removes a pairing token from the URL fragment on load. Over HTTPS or on localhost, a service worker caches the application shell, fonts and icons, never API responses. The interface can then open offline, and you can install it as an app. Saved theme and language apply before the first paint. doona does not download other pages before authentication. Installing an update reuses files already available to the page. See SECURITY.md to report a vulnerability.

title: doona lite
description: doona lite provides forms for common honk configuration tasks.
text: doona lite doona lite provides forms for common honk configuration tasks. It is a preview in testing; see the edition comparison before choosing it for your gateway. Use Nodes, Subscriptions, Groups, Routing and DNS to manage resources, and Settings for global settings. Begin with Connect doona lite, then follow Common tasks.  Install doona lite honk embeds doona lite starting with v0.1.0-beta.4. Install honk as described in Quick start, then add this block to its configuration, replacing any existing native_api block: For a separate installation, use the lite archive in Manual installation; lite has no distribution packages. After either choice, apply the UI restart rule, open the address from Quick start, then connect doona lite. Switch to the standard edition Follow Install and switch editions to select the standard edition's files or embedded UI.

title: Connect doona lite
description: Connect an installed or separately hosted lite page to honk's native API.
text: Connect doona lite Connect an installed or separately hosted lite page to honk's native API. For installation, start with doona lite. 1. Select the backend Open the lite page. If honk serves it, use its /ui/ address. With no saved connection, lite detects honk at the page origin. If honk allows anonymous access, lite connects directly; otherwise it opens the matching sign-in form. Select Use another backend to enter a different address. If lite does not detect honk or you choose another backend: Enter the server root in honk native API root, for example http://192.168.1.1:9527, including any reverse-proxy prefix. Do not include /ui/ or /api/v1, and do not enter a proxy node URL. Select Continue to discover the sign-in method. For a separately hosted page or a hostname, configure hostname and origin access. If discovery fails, check sign-in requirements. 2. Sign in Form Action Set up administrator Enter Username, Password and Confirm password, then select Create and sign in. Use the account format and setup requirements. Sign in Enter the existing honk administrator's Username and Password, then select Sign in. Token field Enter the configured secret in Token, or leave it empty if honk allows anonymous access, then select Connect. After connecting, continue with Common tasks in doona lite. For rejected credentials, use sign-in troubleshooting. Explore without a backend Open the doona lite demo to explore sample data without a backend. Changes to the sample data reset when the page reloads. Release builds of lite connect only to honk and do not offer a demo button.

title: Common tasks in doona lite
description: Import nodes and edit honk configuration after connecting lite.
text: Common tasks in doona lite Import nodes and edit honk configuration after connecting lite. Check configuration write requirements, full validation requirements, and the lite backend requirements if editing is unavailable. Apply a draft After editing a subscription, group, routing, DNS or global setting: Select Review and apply. Check the proposed changes, then select Apply. Wait for Configuration saved and applied., then check the resource again. If the notification reports a failure or unconfirmed result, read it before retrying. Node imports use the immediate apply flow described below. See What doona can change for storage and activation rules. Import nodes from share links Open Nodes and select Add node. Select Paste links and paste one link per line in Share links. Check the recognized nodes and correct invalid lines. Select Add for one node or Add N nodes for several. This writes and applies the nodes immediately; check that they appear in the list. See node requirements and syntax validation if import is unavailable. Add a subscription Open Subscriptions and select Add subscription. Enter Subscription link. Fill in Name (optional) or leave it empty to use the suggested name. Select Save. The new row is a draft. Follow Apply a draft above, then check the subscription's nodes. Editing and deleting subscriptions use the same review flow. For a failed fetch, check subscription refresh requirements. Create a group Open Groups and select Create group. Enter Name, choose Manual choice under Policy, then select Create. In Edit group, find a node under Available nodes and subscriptions and select its Add button. Confirm that it appears under In this group. Follow Apply a draft above, then check the group's members. For group controls, see group editing requirements. Add a domain rule Open Routing and select Add rule. Choose Domain and subdomains, enter example.com in Values, and press Enter. Choose the destination group under Goes to, choose Position, then select Add. Follow Apply a draft above, then check that the domain rule appears. Rebuild rules from a template replaces rules in the draft. Review the replacement before applying it. See rule requirements if editing is unavailable. Add a DNS server Open DNS and select Add DNS server. Choose Custom under Provider, enter a unique Name and a Server address, such as tls://1.1.1.1:853, then select Add. Open the server's Actions menu and select Set as default. Follow Apply a draft above and check the server and default rule. For configuration fields, see Configuration. For write conditions, see rule requirements. Change a global setting Open Settings and choose Sniffing. Set Sniffing timeout to 200 and Duration unit to ms. Follow Apply a draft above, then reopen the setting to check its value. Restart-only settings show read-only values with a Copy button for the configuration line. Copy the line, edit the file's global section on the honk host, then restart honk. Copying the displayed restart command does not execute it. See restart-only global settings and the configuration reference. Share a manual node Open Nodes and find the manually added node. Open its Actions menu and select Share. Select Copy link or scan the QR code. If copying is unavailable, select and copy the displayed link. Subscription nodes do not expose share links here. If a link is too long for a QR code, copy the link. Share links contain connection credentials; share them only with intended recipients.

Restart experimental experimental.native_api.allow_anonymous_loopback false Allows uncredentialed loopback access; does not grant protected writes. Restart experimental experimental.native_api.config_write false Permits source writes and geodata updates with credentials. Restart global global.store_subscribe true Retains subscription bodies for offline startup; per-entry cache must also allow it. Restart experimental experimental.cache_file.store_dns false Retains DNS answers when enabled: true. See revision requirements. Restart experimental experimental.native_api.record_memory true Memory history charts. Restart experimental experimental.native_api.record_flows true Permits flow recording for Routing log and rule-hit evidence. Restart experimental experimental.native_api.record_logs true Permits the Logs recorder. Restart experimental experimental.native_api.record_dns_log true Permits the DNS resolution log recorder. Restart experimental These file keys grant recorder permission. Flows, logs and DNS logs start in on-demand mode. Their runtime switches cannot override a configured prohibition. Connections lists active userspace connections separately from the flow recorder. See Connections, flows, and runtime overrides. Health checks Key Default What doona does with it Applies honk reference global.tcp_check_url https://www.gstatic.com/generate_204 Global HTTP probe target list; the health loop uses the first URL. Restart global global.tcp_check_http_method HEAD Global HTTP health-check method. Restart global global.udp_check_dns dns.google:53, 8.8.8.8, 2001:4860:4860::8888 UDP probe targets; the first literal IP takes precedence over names. Restart global global.check_interval 30s Global health-check interval. Restart global global.check_tolerance 50ms Default latency improvement required to switch URLTest members. Reload global Logging Key Default What doona does with it Applies honk reference global.log_level info Startup filter. A valid RUST_LOG takes precedence, then --debug. Restart global global.log_file '' Optional file output. Relative paths resolve below data_dir; --log-file overrides this value. Restart global Interfaces and kernel Key Default What doona does with it Applies honk reference global.lan_interface [] LAN interfaces for forwarded traffic; no LAN hooks when empty. Restart global global.wan_interface [] Interfaces for host traffic; auto follows the lowest-metric IPv4 default route. Restart global global.tproxy_port 12345 Transparent TCP/UDP listener port. Restart global global.so_mark_from_dae 0 Effective mark is 0x100 at zero; otherwise the configured socket bypass mark. Restart global global.nfqueue_enable true Requests NFQUEUE staging for ambiguous forwarded LAN UDP. Requires the real eBPF backend. Restart global To handle LAN clients, set global.lan_interface to the interface facing them: On a main router, use its LAN bridge, commonly br-lan; clients already use this router as their gateway. On a side router, also set clients' gateway and DNS to the side router's LAN address, either on each client or through the main router's DHCP settings. Do not assume lan_interface: auto selects the LAN. It selects the interface with the lowest-metric IPv4 default route, usually the WAN interface on a main router. Reload global global.udp_warm_node_count 0 UDP warm-up candidate count; zero disables it. Reload global global.preconnect_node_count auto Startup-only bare-TCP warm-up; auto chooses at most eight eligible nodes. Reload does not repeat it. Restart global global.disable_waiting_network false Stored only; does not alter startup waiting. Reload global global.bandwidth_max_tx '' Stored only; does not limit transmit bandwidth. Reload global global.bandwidth_max_rx '' Stored only; does not limit receive bandwidth. Reload global global.utls_imitate chrome_auto Accepted fingerprint request; does not change the single supported Chrome profile. Reload global DNS listener and Clash compatibility Key Default What doona does with it Applies honk reference dns.bind '' Standalone DNS listener; empty disables it. Edit outside doona. Restart dns experimental.clash_api.external_controller '' Clash API listener; empty disables it. Restart experimental experimental.clash_api.external_ui '' Clash dashboard directory. Restart experimental experimental.clash_api.secret '' Clash bearer secret; declaring it makes its source read-only in doona. Restart experimental experimental.clash_api.default_mode Rule Initial Clash mode: Rule, Global, or Direct. Live api dns_log.max_records 512 DNS log capacity; 64–512. Live api flows.max_flows 1024 Flow record capacity; 64–1024. Live api flows.retention_seconds 300 Terminal flow retention; 1–300 seconds. Live api Change these through Settings, not a DAE file. An accepted activation or restart resets them. See runtime override requirements. Live, stored api geodata.verify_checksum true Checksum verification for downloads. Live, stored api geodata.auto_update.enabled true Enables scheduled update checks. Live, stored api geodata.auto_update.interval_hours 24 Interval between scheduled checks, in hours. Live, stored api Change these through Settings with credentials and an available state database. title: What doona can change
description: doona changes configuration sources, runtime state, persistent geodata settings, and browser preferences through different controls.
headings: Accepted fields without the expected live effect
text: What doona can change doona changes configuration sources, runtime state, persistent geodata settings, and browser preferences through different controls. Turning off experimental.native_api.config_write disables configuration writes; it does not disable every action. Where changes are stored In this table, source permission means experimental.native_api.config_write: true, token or password authentication, an available configuration coordinator, and a complete, writable source. A blocked database configuration store also prevents ordinary source edits. Includes follow the same source rules as the main file. Live changes take effect without reloading the configuration. Reload means the write must pass validation and complete its activation operation. Restart means you must edit the configuration outside doona and restart honk. Change Condition Storage and application Source text: node, subscription, group, routing, dns except bind, reloadable global fields, and assets.subscription Source permission. Current revision. Required local dependencies available. File replacement in file mode; a stored revision with --store db. Write plus reload. Add or delete managed nodes and providers Writable main source and the corresponding can_manage capability Write plus reload. Managed deletion excludes built-in nodes, provider-derived nodes, and declarations in includes. Edit a subscription declaration Writable, complete source containing the declaration Source write plus reload. Group fields: policy, default, final, tolerance, idle_timeout, interrupt_connections, check_url Writable owning source, groups.config_patch, and the field in the group's mutable_config Write plus reload. Supports writable includes. The API names default and final as default_member_id and final_outbound. Runtime record_flows, record_logs, record_dns_log, log.level, log.buffered_records, dns_log.max_records, flows.max_flows, flows.retention_seconds Admitted API request; advertised field; configured recorder permission and value bounds Live. No config_write requirement. Restart or an accepted configuration activation resets these overrides. Geodata URL lists, download route, checksum verification, automatic-update schedule, and reset Credentials. Available state database. Corresponding settings advertised. Live, stored in the state database. The settings request does not download or activate files and does not require config_write. doona starts a separate update after saving source URLs when updates are available. Update geodata files Configuration-write authority, credentials, loaded assets with paths and URLs Download, file replacement, then activation. See geodata update requirements. Select a group member, pin an automatic policy, or clear a pin Running backend; group selection capability and the group's can_select or can_override Live runtime action. No source write or config_write requirement. Selector persistence depends on the state cache and experimental.cache_file.enabled not being false. Appearance, language, layout, flag overrides, and probe preferences Browser support and storage Live in this browser. They do not modify honk configuration. Wallpaper persistence uses IndexedDB. Explicit geodata URLs and download routes in the startup configuration replace the corresponding stored overrides when honk starts. A source edit that changes their resolved native API settings requires a restart. See geodata settings. Settings that require a restart The API refuses these effective changes before writing. Use an external editor, then follow Service management. The editor may show a restart-required diagnostic or listener_settings_changed; see write refusals. Section Restart-only keys dns bind global check_interval, tcp_check_url, tcp_check_http_method, udp_check_dns, tls_implementation, tproxy_port, tproxy_port_protect, pprof_port, so_mark_from_dae, log_level, log_file, lan_interface, wan_interface, auto_config_kernel_parameter, data_dir, store_subscribe, nfqueue_enable experimental.native_api Every field, including authentication, listener, UI, recording, and write settings experimental.clash_api external_controller, external_ui, external_ui_download_url, external_ui_download_detour, secret, default_mode experimental.cache_file enabled, store_dns assets geodata.geosite, geodata.geoip, geodata.route, ui.url, ui.route, and inherited route when they change the resolved native or Clash API settings The health-check comparison uses the effective first HTTP URL and method, and the selected UDP DNS target. tls_implementation requires a restart when switching into or out of UTLS mode. The log-file comparison uses the effective path, including any command-line override. The reload policy also compares internal global.tproxy_mark. honk does not accept it as a DAE configuration key; do not add it to your file. honk rejects global.data_dir as listener_settings_changed in database mode and as a restart-required diagnostic in file mode. Why a source is read-only Check the source badge on Configuration. A source can be read-only because: config_write is off, or neither secret nor password_auth provides credentials. It declares a native API or Clash API listener secret. Its text contains a listener-secret value subject to masking. honk masks matching values of at least eight bytes. In database mode, failure to record the active revision blocks the store. Configuration actions also remain unavailable while the source set or write coordinator is unavailable. doona refuses incomplete source content. A write cannot introduce a listener secret, change the set of credential-bearing sources, or change listener settings. Keep listener secrets in a separate include and edit that include outside doona. After restarting honk, reopen Configuration and check the other sources' badges. Separating a secret declaration does not help if another source contains the same masked secret value. See read-only sources and write refusals. Filesystem requirements A writable badge does not prove that the filesystem permits replacement. In file mode, honk must read the original and create and sync a temporary file beside it. It then renames that file over the original and syncs the directory. Its service user needs access to the containing directories and permission to create and replace entries there. Configuration writes reject symbolic links in the source path and nonregular files. A missing write bit on the source file alone is not the permission test: replacement changes the directory entry. Concurrent file changes can also reject the write. After applying, check that the operation succeeded and the source readback contains your change. Geodata updates have separate destination rules: packaged assets are normally replaced by a file in the data directory. See geodata locations. Accepted fields without the expected live effect Field Actual behavior global.preconnect_node_count Consumed by startup warm-up. An accepted source edit does not rerun that warm-up. Restart honk to use the new value for startup. global.tls_fragment, global.tls_fragment_length, global.tls_fragment_interval Accepted and stored for compatibility; no runtime fragmentation consumer in this honk revision. global.bandwidth_max_tx, global.bandwidth_max_rx Accepted and stored for compatibility; no runtime bandwidth-limiting consumer in this honk revision. An accepted edit only starts an operation. The change is active when the operation reaches succeeded; read the source back to confirm it. Even then, a compatibility field does not change traffic behavior.

text: Feature requirements Find your standard-edition feature in the table, then use its section to check prerequisites and enable it. Compare the listed capabilities with System status → Backend features before changing your configuration.
