A missing resource is unavailable; installing a newer UI alone cannot provide it. Settings → Temporary runtime overrides changes only advertised fields. For storage and activation rules, see What doona can change. Error codes identify API failures. The sections distinguish them from read-only reasons, runtime degradation codes, and geodata operation stages. A disabled button can explain a local prerequisite without sending a request or producing an API error. Sign-in and administrator setup Needs A compatible honk build, an enabled native API, and its configured sign-in method. In experimental.native_api, password mode needs password_auth: true and a working state database; token mode uses secret. Initial administrator setup accepts only loopback, private, or link-local peers. Check in doona The sign-in page shows whether you need setup, a password, or a token. System status shows the engine and backend features. To enable Enable enabled: true and your sign-in method in experimental.native_api outside doona. For hostname access, configure the permitted host and browser origin, then restart honk. Follow First sign-in from the gateway or LAN. Check the engine and backend features on System status. Errors Sign-in failures: setup_required, setup_already_completed, invalid_credentials, authentication_required, permission_denied. If the API is absent, see missing native API. Configuration sources, forms, and outbound mode Needs Reading needs config.available and a loaded source set within the backend's byte and source-count limits. Editing needs config.writable, config_write: true in experimental.native_api, credentials, complete source content, and a writable owning source. Creation needs config.create and a path loaded by an include pattern. Global settings and module forms need support from the detected engine. The honk outbound-mode control edits the main source; Global mode also needs an outbound target. Check in doona Configuration shows source badges, diagnostics, and disabled-action explanations. Activity shows the honk outbound-mode control. To enable Enable config_write: true and credentials in experimental.native_api outside doona, then restart honk. Resolve the source's read-only reason. Keep listener secrets in a separate file. Apply your change and check both operation success and source readback. Errors Write failures: stale_revision, state_conflict, permission_denied. Refusal reasons: writes_disabled, configuration_unavailable, listener_secret_source, listener_secret_in_content, listener_settings_changed, unsafe_path. For missing local dependencies, see offline dependencies. Details An external edit can invalidate the revision used by a pending write. Outbound mode is a configuration change, not a separate runtime switch. Configuration validation Needs config_validate.available, the advertised full mode, and an admitted control request. The complete effective source set must fit the validation limits, including locally resolved includes. You can validate main and included sources. Check in doona Check the editor's Validate button and Configuration diagnostics. To enable If full validation is absent, use a backend that implements it. Restore missing includes or geodata dependencies, then select Validate again. Check that the result has no error diagnostics. Validation does not apply your draft. Errors Request errors: request_too_large, invalid_request. For offline-dependency diagnostics, see dependency failures. Export, import, and revisions Needs Export: config_export.available. Import: config_import.available; honor replace_required. List revisions: config_revisions.available. Restore: also can_activate. In honk, import and revisions need --store db; file mode can still export. Import needs an editable configuration store. Check in doona Configuration → Backups and revisions shows the controls for the separate x-honk capabilities. To enable Select the intended storage mode at startup, then refresh Backups and revisions. Import or restore, wait for the operation, and verify the active configuration. If the result is unknown, refresh the original operation before retrying. Errors The import_entry_changed refusal and configuration validation failures can occur. See write refusals. Details You can restore the recorded head when a failed revision record blocks ordinary writes, provided you have configuration-write authority. System status and live metrics Needs System status: runtime. Memory: runtime_memory and each advertised metric. Outbound counters: runtime_outbounds. Datapath details: datapath and the advertised detail kinds. Check in doona Check the Engine, Memory, Datapath, and Backend features cards on System status. To enable Use a compatible backend and resolve the degradation shown by the affected card. Refresh and check that the expected readings appear. Do not treat a missing metric as zero. Errors Counter reads: temporarily_unavailable. See native API access and state database failures. Authentication failures use the common sign-in codes. Details Your backend can provide basic runtime status while some measurements are unavailable. Traffic and memory history Needs Traffic history: traffic_history.available and record_traffic: true in experimental.native_api. Memory history: memory_history.available and record_memory: true in experimental.native_api. Check in doona Check the traffic and memory charts on Activity and System status, and their entries in Backend features. To enable Enable the corresponding recorder in experimental.native_api outside doona, then restart honk. Allow samples to accumulate and verify that the chart gains samples. Errors An unavailable history endpoint returns capability_not_supported. See backend compatibility. Details The recorders are independent startup settings, not runtime switches. The backend advertises maximum windows and sample counts. A bounded ring can retain less than the maximum window. Nodes and subscription declarations Needs Lists: nodes.available and providers.available. Managed creation and deletion: the corresponding can_manage and a writable main source. Subscription editing: a unique declaration, honk source syntax, and a complete, writable owning source. Creation options such as update interval, User-Agent, and cache must appear in providers.create_options. Check in doona On Nodes, inspect the Add, Edit, and Delete explanations. To enable Resolve source permissions. For write permission, enable config_write: true and credentials in experimental.native_api outside doona, then restart honk. Apply your change and verify the resulting entry. Refresh a newly created honk provider to load its nodes; it starts unfetched. Errors capability_not_supported, state_conflict, unsupported_value. See write refusals. Details Managed deletion excludes built-in nodes, provider-derived nodes, and declarations owned by includes. You also cannot delete a node referenced as a group's final outbound through managed deletion. Subscription refresh Needs providers.can_refresh, operations.available, and a refreshable provider. In honk, a running subscription supervisor and an enabled subscription. The backend must be running when it admits the operation. Check in doona Nodes shows the refresh action, provider status, node count, and last error. To enable Enable the subscription and check its URL and download route. Refresh it, wait for the operation, and verify its updated status and nodes. Errors capability_not_supported, state_conflict, temporarily_unavailable, resource_not_found. For an unavailable backend, see native API access. Provider error route_unavailable: its selected route has no usable node. For activation dependency failures, see offline dependencies. Details The built-in inline provider is not a subscription to download. Group listing, selection, and pins Needs Policies: groups.available. Selection: the group selection capability and can_select. Pinning or clearing an automatic-policy override: can_override. A running backend. These actions do not require config_write or edit the source. Check in doona Check the group's controls on Policies. To enable Choose a selectable group or a policy that allows overrides. Select or clear a member and verify the selected member or override indicator. Errors state_conflict, resource_not_found. For API access failures, see sign-in failures. If the selection disappears after restart, check persistence requirements. Group creation, editing, and check settings Needs Creation: a complete, writable main source. Editing: loaded configuration and exactly one declaration in a complete, writable source. Missing, duplicate, or incomplete declarations disable Edit even with configuration-write permission. Group check settings: groups.config_patch and the requested field in mutable_config. See the field list in What doona can change. Check in doona Policies explains why Edit or a field is unavailable. To enable Resolve duplicate declarations outside the group editor or restore complete source readback. If configuration writes are off, enable config_write: true and credentials in experimental.native_api outside doona, then restart honk. Apply your change and verify the group's configuration after activation. Errors Revision conflicts: stale_revision, state_conflict. For source refusals, see read-only sources. Details Source editing and the restricted group PATCH controls have different prerequisites. Latency probes Needs probes.available and a compatible intersection of advertised target types, probe kinds, transports, and IP families. Your group must support every requested transport. Each selected node's protocol must support the probe kind and transport, including in a mixed selection. Check in doona Check Settings → Latency probes and the probe controls on Nodes or Policies. To enable Choose an offered probe and IP family. Run the probe and check its per-kind result. Errors Request refusals: unsupported_value, rate_limited, temporarily_unavailable. Transport failures appear in the probe result. For missing probe support, see native API compatibility. Details If your saved choice no longer fits the target, doona selects HTTP if available, otherwise the first compatible choice. doona cannot offer a probe when the intersection is empty. Connections and closing traffic Needs Listing: connections.available. Closing: can_close, an admitted control request, and a connection whose transfer belongs to userspace. Bulk close must fit the advertised maximum number of matching entries. Check in doona Check Connections and its close-action explanations. To enable Generate traffic through the configured interface and verify an entry appears. Close an eligible connection and confirm it leaves the live list. Errors state_conflict, resource_not_found, request_too_large. See Connections or Rules stay empty. Details The list shows connections that honk handles in userspace. Traffic the kernel forwards directly, such as direct traffic, does not appear. Flows and recorded rule hits Needs flows.available, record_flows: true in experimental.native_api, and an active recording policy. Check recording.flows.active in runtime settings. Availability alone does not mean capture is active. Check in doona Check Routing log, Rules' recorded hits, and Settings → Temporary runtime overrides. To enable If configuration prohibits recording, enable record_flows: true in experimental.native_api outside doona and restart honk. Choose an offered runtime mode. Generate new traffic and verify a recorded flow. Existing traffic does not prove that the recorder captured it. Errors Reads: snapshot_expired, snapshot_unavailable, flow_expired. Refresh the view for a new snapshot. For an empty view, see empty connection and rule lists. Details Off records nothing; On records supported scopes; Auto records on client demand; Sampled records a subset. Routing rules, DNS rules, and templates Needs Lists: rules.available or dns_rules.available. Adding, editing, or holding a rule: source permission and a locatable rule or insertion position. Routing templates: honk syntax, a complete writable target, routing confined to one source, valid referenced groups, and valid local geodata dependencies. Service rules: rules.available, config.available and a writable fallback rule. The rules go into the fallback's file. Check in doona Rules and DNS rules show unavailable actions and dependency explanations. To enable Resolve the owning source. If configuration writes are off, enable config_write: true and credentials in experimental.native_api outside doona, then restart honk. Use a single routing source before applying a template. After activation, check the rule list and trace a matching destination. Errors Source write refusals: see read-only sources. Dependency diagnostics: missing-offline-dependency, unreadable-offline-dependency, invalid-offline-dependency. See offline dependencies. Routing trace Needs routing_trace.available, a supported resolution mode, and valid query inputs. The backend must advertise live resolution in resolve_modes. Your trace must fit backend request and time limits. Check in doona Open the trace panel on Rules. To enable Install a compatible backend if the trace capability is absent. Choose an offered resolution mode and supply the destination and other requested fields. Run the trace and check its matched steps and final outbound. Errors invalid_request, unsupported_value, request_too_large, temporarily_unavailable. For missing backend support, see native API compatibility. Events Needs events.available. Check in doona Check Events and its connection state. To enable Connect to a backend that advertises the resource. Perform an action such as a reload and verify that its event appears. Errors An old resume cursor can return event_cursor_expired. See missing startup messages. Details The backend advertises event kinds, retention, and client limits. The stream only provides retained events. Reconnecting cannot recover events already evicted from the buffer. Logs Needs logs.available, record_logs: true in experimental.native_api, an active recording mode, and a level that includes your messages. The backend must advertise the filters. Check in doona Check Logs and Settings → Temporary runtime overrides. To enable If necessary, enable record_logs: true in experimental.native_api outside doona and restart honk. Choose an offered recording mode and level. Generate a new event at that level and verify its log entry. Errors capability_not_supported, unsupported_value, event_cursor_expired. See startup messages and recorder limits. Details Buffer capacity and retention limit replay. Use the service log for messages from before the API recorder's installation. DNS queries and upstream selection Needs dns_query.available and an advertised record type. Selecting a named upstream also needs readable configuration containing that upstream. Check in doona DNS → Query shows the offered types and upstreams. To enable If you need to select an upstream explicitly, define it in the dns configuration block, apply, and reopen Query. Choose an offered type and upstream, run a query, and check the response and reported result. Errors Invalid or unsupported requests: invalid_request, unsupported_value. For access failures, see native API access. Details If your selected upstream is missing or removed, doona returns the selection to Automatic. DNS cache actions Needs Listing: dns_cache.available and read. Deleting one entry, deleting a name, and flushing: delete_entry, delete_name, and flush respectively. These are independent capabilities. Check in doona DNS → Cache shows supported controls. To enable Use a backend that advertises the action you need. Enabling DNS logging does not enable cache actions. Delete or flush, then refresh the list and check the result. New DNS traffic can populate it again. Errors Reads: snapshot_expired, snapshot_unavailable. Malformed requests: invalid_request. For compatibility and access, see native API access. DNS log and statistics Needs dns_log.available, record_dns_log: true in experimental.native_api, and an active recorder mode. Query and cache capabilities are separate. Check in doona Check DNS → Log and Statistics, plus Settings → Temporary runtime overrides. To enable If configuration prohibits recording, enable record_dns_log: true in experimental.native_api outside doona and restart honk. Select an offered mode, generate DNS traffic, and verify new log entries and statistics. Errors capability_not_supported, temporarily_unavailable. See recording and startup messages. Details A permitted but inactive recorder produces no new samples. Runtime overrides Needs runtime_settings.available and the requested field in fields. You do not need config_write. Recorder permissions and value bounds must allow your value, even when the backend advertises the recorder-mode field. Check in doona Settings → Temporary runtime overrides shows available controls and recording state. To enable If necessary, enable the corresponding startup recorder in experimental.native_api outside doona and restart honk. Adjust the runtime value and verify the returned setting. Errors Invalid values: invalid_request. Unadvertised or prohibited values: unsupported_value. See write boundaries and backend access failures. Details Restart or an accepted configuration activation resets these overrides. Geodata availability Needs geodata.available and a consistent set of loaded assets across the traffic and DNS routers. Check in doona Settings → Geodata shows loaded assets and status. An asset mismatch can make the resource unavailable. To enable Install the assets your rules require. Reload or restart honk and check the list. Errors An unavailable loaded set can return capability_not_supported. See offline dependency failures. Details Update now updates loaded assets; it does not install missing dependencies. Manual geodata updates Needs geodata.can_update, configuration-write authority, credentials, and at least one loaded asset. Every loaded asset needs a disk path and a usable URL. Use a final HTTP or HTTPS URL; honk rejects redirects. The service user must be able to stage, replace, and sync files in the destination. Check in doona Settings → Geodata shows Update now, asset details, and the operation result. Update now remains disabled until geodata status loads and the current action finishes. To enable Enable config_write: true and credentials in experimental.native_api outside doona if necessary. Set geosite and geoip in assets.geodata for loaded assets. With a working state database, you can set sources through Settings instead. Set route in assets.geodata if needed; it inherits assets.route when unset. For direct hostname downloads, configure a usable bootstrap_resolver in global. Restart honk after editing these startup settings. In Settings → Geodata, select Update now, wait for completion, and check asset details and the operation result. Errors Download stages: download_timeout, checksum_unavailable, checksum_mismatch, http_status_rejected, http_not_found, connection_failed, tls_failed, group_unavailable, route_blocked, asset_too_large, invalid_source. Replacement stages: replacement_failed means replacement failed; directory_sync_failed means honk could not confirm durability and may already have replaced a file. Before retrying, select Copy error on the failure notice. The copied details.assets lists each asset's written and durability_confirmed values; the asset details in Settings do not show them. Check these values and the destination filesystem. Details Manual updates do not need the state database if configuration supplies every loaded asset's URL. Without the database, honk cannot use its stored or built-in URL lists. Each URL attempt uses the selected route. A failed group or routing decision does not fall back to direct. Asset lookup checks DAE_LOCATION_ASSET, then global.data_dir, then legacy locations, the working directory, and share directories. Packaged assets receive a replacement in the data directory, which takes precedence over the packaged copy. honk replaces assets already in the data directory or explicit asset directory in place. Each file download attempt allows 30 seconds without progress and 10 minutes in total. The checksum request has a separate 10-second deadline and appends .sha256sum to the URL path. A checksum 404 leaves the asset unverified. Other checksum fetch failures reject that attempt. An operation can fail after changing some files. Geodata sources, route, checksum, schedule, and reset Needs Credentials and a working state database for every settings write: source URL lists, download route, checksum verification, automatic-update schedule, and reset. You do not need config_write. geodata.configurable_sources and geodata in runtime_settings.fields. Route and checksum controls also need their corresponding returned settings. Selecting a group route needs the groups resource and a current group. Automatic downloads still need the update prerequisites. Check in doona Check Settings → Geodata. If source and schedule controls are absent, inspect the persistence warning on System status. To enable Repair state database access, restart honk, and verify that the controls appear. Save your change and confirm the returned setting. When you change source URLs and updates are available, check the separate update operation that doona starts after saving. Errors Settings failures: permission_denied, capability_not_supported, state_conflict for a stale group, temporarily_unavailable when storage fails. See unavailable geodata controls and unsafe database paths. Details The settings request only stores values. Reset is also a database write, not an edit to your configuration file. Overrides persist in the database, but startup re-seeds explicitly configured geodata URLs and the download route over stored overrides. Operations, reload, suspend, and resume Needs Tracking accepted actions: operations.available. Reload: also reload.available. Suspend: suspend.available and a running backend. Resume: resume.available and a suspended backend. The inspected honk revision advertises Suspend and Resume as unavailable. No configuration switch enables them there. Check in doona Check Settings → Backend and the action's progress or failure notice. To enable Use a compatible backend's supported action, or use Service management for process control. After reload, verify the accepted configuration and runtime state. Errors Operation failures: state_conflict, configuration diagnostics, temporarily_unavailable. See write and operation failures. Details An accepted request does not prove that the operation succeeded. If the result is unknown, read it back before another write. Process-name routing and UDP trace details Needs Process-name routing: cgroup v2 socket identity capture. Full names: kernel argument capture. UDP trace details separately need kernel tracing support. Check in doona System status → Datapath shows reduced-support explanations. To enable Use a kernel and cgroup setup that supports the required hooks. See kernel requirements. Restart honk and verify that the relevant warning clears. A UI setting cannot add a missing kernel hook. Errors Runtime degradation codes: pname_routing_reduced, pname_routing_disabled, udp_trace_unavailable. See kernel failures. These report reduced support; they are not configuration-write errors. Details Without kernel argument capture, honk falls back to the thread's comm name instead of the argument-derived name. Keeping selections and probe history Needs A working state cache, with enabled in experimental.cache_file not set to false, to keep Selector choices and latency history across restarts. This honk revision uses the state database for persistence. Password authentication also needs that database at startup. Check in doona Check the persistence explanation on System status. To enable Leave enabled in experimental.cache_file unset to keep Selector choices and delay samples. Resolve ownership, permissions, unsafe paths, locks, or corruption as described in State database problems. Restart honk and check that the warning is gone before relying on saved state. Errors Runtime degradation codes: state_cache_unavailable, which the UI recognizes, and persistence_unavailable, which honk reports with a reason when it continues without its database. See state database failures. Appearance and browser storage Needs Browser settings do not need configuration-write permission. Liquid Glass needs Chromium with support for SVG-backed backdrop-filter. Wallpaper persistence needs working IndexedDB. Flag overrides need a node name without an embedded flag. Check in doona Check Settings → Appearance and the flag picker. To enable Use a supported browser for Liquid Glass and allow browser storage for persistence. Choose a wallpaper and reopen the page to verify that it persists. To change an embedded flag, change the node's actual name. The browser override cannot replace it. Errors Browser storage failures show local explanations instead of honk API codes. For stale UI assets after an upgrade, see browser refresh. Details Without persistence, doona can keep the wallpaper for your current session.

title: Troubleshooting
description: Find your symptom, then follow its checks and fix.
headings: A control is missing or disabled
A file is read-only, or a write is refused
Apply writes nothing and lists global.nfqueue_enable as needing a restart
Apply says a required file is unavailable
The native API or UI cannot be reached
honk rejects a native API setting at startup
Geodata sources or the update schedule cannot be edited
honk reports a state database failure
The persistence warning has reason unsafe
Traffic fails after stopping OpenWrt's firewall
apk reports breaks: world[…] when installing other packages
Pinning a map fails with Invalid argument
honk rejects the kernel or compiled routing
LAN traffic is not routed as expected
An open tab still shows the previous version
doona lite cannot open, or the wrong edition appears
Collect an error for a report
text: Troubleshooting Find your symptom, then follow its checks and fix. This page covers connection, editing, recording and geodata failures in doona with honk. Symptom Start here A control is missing or disabled Feature controls A file is read-only or Apply fails Configuration writes Sign-in fails Sign-in There is no native API, or /ui/ returns 404 API and UI access Geodata update fails Update errors Geodata source or schedule controls are missing Geodata settings A monitoring page is empty Recording and visibility A control is missing or disabled Open System status and read Features that are off. doona uses the backend's advertised capabilities and the current source or recording state to decide which actions it can offer. Affected action Check and fix Editing files, rules or outbound mode Follow configuration requirements; for a source badge, use read-only files. Adding nodes or subscriptions Follow node management requirements. Refreshing a subscription or measuring latency Check refresh requirements or probe requirements. Selecting a group member or editing a group Selection and editing have separate selection and editing requirements. A recorder or its settings Follow runtime override requirements and the relevant recording checks. A feature the build does not provide Compare the installed engine with supported honk builds. A file is read-only, or a write is refused Open Configuration → Config files and inspect the source's badge or diagnostic. For the complete permission and filesystem rules, see what doona can change and configuration requirements. Reported reason Fix writes_disabled Follow the configuration requirements above to enable authenticated writes. configuration_unavailable Check honk's startup log and wait for its configuration to load before editing. listener_secret_source Edit this secret-bearing file on disk. Keep listener secrets in their own include so other files remain editable. listener_secret_in_content Check for a listener-secret value in the content or path. Replace an overlapping secret outside doona and sign in again after applying the change. listener_settings_changed or a restart-required diagnostic Edit the setting outside doona and follow the restart rules. credential_sources_changed Reload honk after the external credential-file change, then reopen the source before editing. unsafe_path Use a regular file in an allowed configuration directory; check the filesystem requirements. stale_revision or state_conflict after another edit Resolve the changed file before applying again. import_entry_changed Start honk with -c pointing to the active configuration entry before importing server files. If the result is unknown, check the current source before repeating the write. For an accepted import or restore, reopen that action under Backups and revisions. If its dialog still reports an unknown result, select Refresh there to query the original operation. A lost response does not prove the write failed. Apply writes nothing and lists global.nfqueue_enable as needing a restart On a kernel without NFQUEUE support, honk turns NFQUEUE off at startup and logs NFQUEUE is unavailable at startup. honk 0.1.0-beta.4 and earlier then compare every write with the default nfqueue_enable: true, so Apply reports Nothing was written and lists global.nfqueue_enable as a setting that needs a restart, also after a restart. Set the value in the global section, then restart honk: Apply then writes normally. Apply says a required file is unavailable honk validates local dependencies before writing. Inspect the diagnostic and the files referenced by the configuration. The diagnostic does not name the dependency file. For subscription or node errors, check cached subscription content and each node's ech_config_path. For DNS errors, check the files named by use_host. Restore missing files or refresh malformed subscription content, then apply again. Code Cause and fix missing-offline-dependency Restore the missing dependency. For geodata, use installation instructions, or OpenWrt geodata installation. offline-dependency-denied Put the dependency in an allowed configuration or data directory and grant the service user read access. invalid-offline-dependency Replace malformed content, or refresh the affected subscription. unreadable-offline-dependency Check the service log for the underlying file or storage error. Update now updates loaded assets; it cannot install a missing initial asset. Check geodata requirements before applying again. Sign-in fails Check sign-in requirements, then match the response below. Symptom or code Cause and fix setup_required Complete administrator setup through First sign-in. setup_already_completed An administrator already exists. Sign in with that account. invalid_credentials Re-enter the account credentials. For a forgotten password, use the reset steps below. authentication_required Sign in again using the authentication method configured for this backend. permission_denied during setup Check the allowed client addresses in setup requirements. A network error or HTTP 403 through a hostname or another origin Check reachability, then follow hostname and origin access. The API is reachable but denies a protected action Check that action's feature requirements, including credentials and write authority. Reset a forgotten administrator password On the gateway, stop honk. Run the installed honk-core as its service user, replacing /var/lib/honk with the data directory from your configuration: If you are unsure which directory to pass, follow the data-directory checks. The command deletes the administrator record and reports whether one existed. Start honk again, then follow First sign-in to create the administrator. The native API or UI cannot be reached Use the startup log from the current service run to identify the running build and listener. Check compatible builds and API configuration. Symptom Cause and fix Connection to the listener fails Check that honk is running and the enabled API listens at the address you opened. Use service checks. native API listener bind failed Confirm that listen names an address on this gateway and that another process is not using the port. Subscription HTTP client creation failed, followed by subscription network startup failed Read the underlying TLS error and check the system CA certificate store. Install your distribution's certificate package, such as ca-certificates or OpenWrt's ca-bundle. command not found or a missing executable Compare the honk-core path with your platform's installation instructions. /api returns 404 or sign-in shows This honk build has no native API Confirm the address points to honk, then install a build that provides the native API. Only /ui/ returns 404 Check the configured UI path and the files installed there. Follow UI installation. Startup reports failed to inspect native UI directory, failed to inspect native UI index.html or native UI index.html must be a regular file Correct the UI directory or extract the UI files so its index.html is a readable regular file. An action returns capability_not_supported Use System status to check that specific feature. This code alone does not mean the whole API is absent. honk rejects a native API setting at startup native API setting belongs inside native_api { } means the field sits directly under experimental. Compare your file with the native API configuration and move the field into the nested block. enabled and secret belong to several experimental blocks. Placing either directly under experimental produces unknown experimental setting without naming a single destination block. Move native API fields into native_api { }. unknown experimental setting can also mean the running build does not support the setting. native-api feature is required means the build lacks the enabled native API feature. Check the running build against honk requirements. For authentication combinations rejected at startup, use the exact startup error with sign-in requirements and the configuration reference. A geodata update fails Open Settings → Geodata and read the failed operation's stage. If Update now is missing or disabled, start with update requirements. Stage What to check or change checksum_unavailable The checksum request failed. Check the mirror's checksum URL or choose another source. checksum_mismatch The downloaded content and checksum differ. Obtain a matching file and checksum from the source. download_timeout Check the download route and source; see the download deadlines. http_status_rejected Check the server's status and use a final URL rather than a redirect. http_not_found Correct the file URL. connection_failed Check the chosen route and node; for a direct hostname download, check the resolver described in update requirements. tls_failed Check the gateway clock and the server certificate and hostname. group_unavailable Check the selected group's usable nodes on Policies. route_blocked Correct the routing rule that sends this download to block. asset_too_large Check that the URL supplies the intended geodata file. invalid_source Correct the source URL. replacement_failed or directory_sync_failed Inspect the per-asset result and destination filesystem before retrying; follow replacement requirements. See update requirements for checksum 404 handling, verification and partial-write behavior. Geodata sources or the update schedule cannot be edited Check System status → Datapath for a persistence warning. A persistence_unavailable degradation means the state database is unavailable; use its reason with the database checks. Restore geodata settings requirements, then reopen the Geodata card. Manual downloads have separate requirements; their availability does not prove that honk can save settings. honk reports a state database failure Read the latest startup error in the service log. Password authentication requires the database. If honk cannot open it, startup stops. In file-based token mode, some failures leave honk running without persistence; see persistence requirements. Message or reason Next action unavailable Check that the service user can create and access the configured data directory and its state directory. unsafe Follow unsafe path checks. Locked by honk-core admin reset Wait for that command to finish before starting honk. Another honk-core has the database open Stop the conflicting instance before starting this one. Foreign application ID or newer schema Use the honk build that owns this database; do not overwrite it with an older build. corrupt In file-based token mode, honk moves a corrupt database to state/honk.db.corrupt under the data directory and creates a new database. It never overwrites an earlier corrupt copy, including state/honk.db.corrupt-wal. Preserve any blocking copies elsewhere before restarting. After repairing access, restart the service and check whether the persistence warning is gone. The persistence warning has reason unsafe The service log names the refused path, rule and suggested fix. Check that exact path with the data-directory configuration; do not assume every installation uses the same directory. In file mode, global.data_dir selects the runtime data directory; --data-dir does not override it. Pass that same directory to --data-dir for admin reset. On OpenWrt, /var is volatile; use the manual installation’s persistent directory. The state directory and database must belong to honk's service user and exclude group and other permissions. honk also refuses a symlink or the wrong file type. Correct only the named path's ownership, permissions or type, then restart honk. Do not apply recursive permission changes to the configuration directory. Traffic fails after stopping OpenWrt's firewall If stopping the firewall removes honk's nftables table, start the firewall again, then run /etc/init.d/honk-core restart on the gateway. The firewall manager must leave inet honk_nfqueue and its udp_decision chain intact while honk runs. apk reports breaks: world[…] when installing other packages apk pins a package installed from a file, such as doona or honk downloaded as an .apk, to that file in /etc/apk/world. Once a repository carries another version, every apk add fails, even for unrelated tools, with an error such as honk-0.1.0_beta2-r1: breaks: world[honk><Q1…]. To follow the daeuniverse feed, run apk add honk@daeuniverse, listing any other packages in the same command. To keep the local build, name its file again in the same apk add command. Pinning a map fails with Invalid argument Check the bpffs mount at /sys/fs/bpf; follow kernel and filesystem requirements. honk rejects the kernel or compiled routing Check the minimum kernel version and BPF/BTF support in Requirements. Keep the full verifier log when reporting a verifier failure. LAN traffic is not routed as expected Check the LAN interface instructions, including the bridge name and the client gateway and DNS settings for a side router. Connections or Rules stay empty Empty view Cause and next check Connections Clear filters and read any visibility or truncation notice. Check connection coverage; a missing row does not establish that traffic stopped. Routing log or recorded rule hits Check flow recording. Resolution log or DNS statistics Check DNS recording. Logs Check log recording. The recorder cannot recover earlier startup messages; read the service log. Events Check event availability and the selected kind filter. Log recording defaults to On log demand. In demand mode, each permitted recorder starts when a client requests its data, with a 60-second grace period after demand ends. Connections, Rules and Routing log request flow recording while open. For how each view uses its data, see Watching traffic. An open tab still shows the previous version Reload the page after upgrading. When doona reports that a new version is ready, select Reload. With ui: embedded, the bundled UI comes from the installed honk binary; check the UI setting in the configuration reference. doona lite cannot open, or the wrong edition appears Check the directory and extracted files against lite installation. After changing the UI setting, follow the native API restart rule, then reload the browser page. For HTTP 403 or origin failures, use sign-in checks. Collect an error for a report Select Copy error in the failure notice, or Copy recent errors under Settings → About. Include the action you attempted and the running engine and UI versions. Copy the error before reloading the page, which clears the in-memory error history. The history retains at most 20 errors. Copied details include request method and path, status, error code and request ID when available. The copy omits request bodies and configuration text, and redacts recognized secret fields. See About for the copy actions.

title: Development
description: Build and check doona locally.
headings: Capture screenshots and check the API
text: Development Build and check doona locally. The app lives in Zakkaus/doona; these pages and their site live in Zakkaus/doona-docs. Read the app's CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting changes. For tool versions, see Requirements. Build the standard edition From the doona app repository root: The development server uses the mock backend. Stop it before continuing with the build and checks: The build writes dist/. check runs type checks, lint, translation and formatting checks, unit tests, and generated API checks. check:size measures the built output. Build doona lite From the same app repository root, after installing the root dependencies: The build writes apps/lite/dist/. Use pnpm --dir apps/lite dev to start its development server. Run browser tests From the app repository root: The first command installs the browsers and system dependencies. The second rebuilds the standard edition and runs Playwright tests. For a live backend, set DOONA_API to its server root, supply DOONA_TOKEN through your shell environment if required, and run pnpm e2e:live. This runs the accessibility, mobile and keyboard specifications. Keep credentials out of command history and reports. Live tests reject backend overrides in fixture storage and block control requests, including DNS queries. Ordinary pnpm e2e rejects DOONA_API unless you set DOONA_LIVE_OBSERVE=1; use pnpm e2e:live for the supported live-backend pass. Capture screenshots and check the API Run these tools from the app repository root after installing its dependencies. Screenshots: install Playwright's Chromium, cwebp and img2webp, then start a mock-backed preview. Run node tools/screenshots.mjs <url> docs/screenshots, replacing <url> with the preview address. The tool writes localized pages, a palette sheet, an English theme gallery, phone strips, page-tour stills and a routing animation as WebP. API contract: run node tools/conformance.mjs http://router:9527, replacing the address with the backend's server root. It checks discovery, capabilities and read-only responses against the vendored contract, skipping mutating operations. If the backend requires authentication, pass the token from your shell environment with --token "$DOONA_TOKEN". Package both editions Build both editions first. Install GNU tar, gzip, Brotli and sha256sum, then run from the app repository root: The release/ directory contains the standard, lite, fonts and precompressed archives, plus SHA256SUMS. Archive names use package.json's version. pnpm package --git-version uses git describe --tags --always without a leading v.
